observations:
Torah #250 is a unified, single-cluster teaching. The entire bechina subgraph from the dataset forms one connected component of 4 nodes (השגחה, תפלה, גדול, דמעות). There is no independent domain of 3 or more bechina-connected nodes outside this package.

The source text does introduce an evil/natural counter-domain — הטבע (nature), מזל (fate), and the עכו"ם (nations) who operate under this domain — but these are never connected to each other by explicit bechina language in the Torah. The nations/nature domain functions as the backdrop and foil of the teaching, not as a structured bechina cluster. Specifically:
- הטבע is always described as what prayer/hashgacha transcend or negate (eitza relationship), not as bechina-equivalent to another concept.
- ים הגדול is called a bechina of עכו"ם (one pair, two nodes) — insufficient to form a standalone package by the rule of 3+ nodes.
- מזל and כוכבים are mentioned as part of the natural order that hashgacha overrides, but no bechina equalities are stated between them.

The gap candidates (ראות, נסים) identified in the additions file are extensions of Package 1, not seeds of a new package. They are bechina-equivalent to השגחה and would join Package 1 if added to the dataset.

Conclusion: The single package (הַשְׁגָּחָה וּתְפִלָּה) adequately covers the complete bechina topology of Torah #250. No new package is warranted.
